item.title: Cowboys stressing discipline, communication ahead of matchup with Lamar Jackson
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys defense has had a hard time keeping quarterbacks from making plays with their legs through the first two weeks of the season and they'll face another player capable of hurting them in that area this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys defense has had a hard time keeping quarterbacks from making plays with their legs through the first two weeks of the season and they'll face another player capable of hurting them in that area this week.

Lamar Jackson will be on the other side of the line when the Cowboys take on the Ravens in Brazil this Sunday and the Ravens are surely aware that the Cowboys have allowed an average of 6.6 yards every time a quarterback has run with the ball this season. Finding a way to keep Jackson from having the same kind of success is central to the Cowboys' preparation this week and defensive tackle Kenny Clark identified the key facets to the team's approach.

"Just being disciplined," Clark said, via the team's website. "Communication, just understanding our rush lanes, playing with extension, powering offensive linemen and just restricting those gaps so you can't get through. But the main thing is just staying disciplined and communicating."

The Cowboys' job will be made more difficult by the presence of Derrick Henry in the Ravens' backfield, so defensive coordinator Christian Parker will have his work cut out for him when it comes to improving on the team's underwhelming defensive performance so far this season.

item.title: The 2024 Seahawks did indeed have one specific Michigan influence
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The story of the day on Tuesday featured the unexpected disclosure of a behind-the-scenes beef between the Seahawks and Broncos.
item.content:encoded:
The story of the day on Tuesday featured the unexpected disclosure of a behind-the-scenes beef between the Seahawks and Broncos. And while the whole thing was eye opening (and likely not intended for air), one specific line caught my eye.

Regarding Broncos coach Sean Payton's assertion that the Seahawks had obtained training-camp footage through improper means, Macdonald said, "He thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant."

That's a reference to the 2023 Connor Stalions scandal in Ann Arbor, where Stalions developed a mechanism (in violation of NCAA rules) to scout future opponents with the goal of figuring out their sideline signals. In this specific context, Payton presumably suggested that the Seahawks sent someone to Broncos training camp to record their plays.

Beyond the fact that Macdonald's journey included a year on Jim Harbaugh's Michigan staff (2021, as defensive coordinator), the 2024 Seahawks employed former Michigan assistant Matt Weiss as an outside consultant. And while Weiss's coaching career has imploded due to criminal allegations of widespread hacking, it's fair to point out that the 2024 Seahawks had a distinct Michigan component.

That's not to say Payton's allegations had any merit. Faced with a threat that the Seahawks would sue the Broncos if Payton went public with his suspicions of shenanigans, the issue died. And it would have remained unknown if Macdonald had spoken about it into a hot mic.

It will be interesting to hear what Macdonald and Payton have to say about it today, when they meet with reporters for their usual Wednesday press conferences. Regardless of their likely efforts to downplay the situation and move on, the Seahawks have self-applied the kind of scarlet letter that will give the coaches of the teams they beat the same kind of excuse that plagued the Patriots during their run of dominance.

Pressed by owners as to why the Seahawks keep beating their teams, coaches can resort to the notion that the Seahawks cheat. Even without a shred of evidence to support that claim.

If/when that happens, it will trace to the fact that Macdonald got way too comfortable — and said way too much about a topic that otherwise would have never come to light.

Meanwhile, the Broncos host the Seahawks in 22 days, for a Thursday night game. Which will create a motivation for multiple media outles to fully explore the rabbit hole that, as of Tuesday morning, no one even knew existed.

item.title: Panthers place RB Jonathon Brooks on IR, sign Isaiah Simmons to 53-man roster
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Panthers have made a couple of roster moves official.
item.content:encoded:
The Panthers have made a couple of roster moves official.

With news emerging that Jonathon Brooks will undergo core muscle surgery, Carolina has placed the running back on injured reserve.

He will reportedly miss at least six weeks.

As a corresponding move, the Panthers have signed safety Isaiah Simmons to the 53-man roster from the club’s practice squad.

Carolina had elevated Simmons to the gameday roster for each of the first two games. He has played 80 percent of the club’s special teams snaps.

The Panthers will be on the road to face the Browns in Week 3.

item.title: Mike Macdonald recounts "Cold War" with Sean Payton over cheating suspicions during the 2024 season
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Week 6 game between the Broncos and Seahawks has gained a new subplot.
item.content:encoded:
The Week 6 game between the Broncos and Seahawks has gained a new subplot.

During an appearance on In Depth with Graham Bensinger, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald recounted a story involving Broncos head coach Sean Payton from his first season in Seattle. The Seahawks played the Broncos in Week 1 that year and Macdonald said that the team's staff collected fan videos posted to social media from Broncos practices as part of their preparation because they were "public knowledge."

The Seahawks won 26-20 and Macdonald said Payton "got wind of" how they used the videos in the middle of the season. Payton called Seahawks General Manager John Schneider and, per Macdonald, "lost it."

"He basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriot Spygate type of thing," Macdonald said. "I'm sitting there like, 'Oh my god. We didn't cheat.' They thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant and the whole thing. So we had to counter with him and say, 'If you come out with this, we're going to sue you because it's not true.'"

Macdonald said that Payton eventually dropped the issue, but that it felt like the two teams were involved in something more geopolitical than football until that happened.

"It was like the Cold War," Macdonald said. "He's like, 'I'm going to hit the button. I'm going to hit the button.' 'Well, we're going to hit the button.' None of us hit the button."

Macdonald said he and Payton subsequently crossed paths at the Scouting Combine, but the issue didn't come up. Payton will likely be asked about his version of events at some point before the Week 6 meeting between the teams.

item.title: Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks needs surgery, out at least six weeks
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The groin injury suffered by Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks on Sunday was worse than initially believed.
item.content:encoded:
The groin injury suffered by Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks on Sunday was worse than initially believed.

Although Brooks was initially described as week-to-week, he will actually miss at least six weeks, according to Ian Rapoport.

Brooks is scheduled for core muscle surgery today. The Panthers will put him on injured reserve.

At this point, it's more newsworthy when Brooks is healthy than when he's injured. The Panthers made him the first running back selected in the 2024 NFL draft while he was still recovering from a torn ACL in college, he tore the same ACL as a rookie, and he didn't play at all in 2025.

Brooks has just 52 yards on 18 carries in his career. He still has never so much as gained a single rushing first down.

item.title: Tyson Bagent placed in concussion protocol, putting Case Keenum in line to start Week 3
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Chicago is dealing with multiple injuries at quarterback. The club will play Philadelphia on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
As it turns out, Chicago's backup quarterback is also dealing with an injury.

Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Tyson Bagent has been diagnosed with a concussion and is now in the protocol.

With starter Caleb Williams week-to-week with a hamstring injury, Case Keenum is now in line to start against the Eagles next Monday night.

Bagent entered Sunday’s 9-3 loss to the Vikings midway through the fourth quarter after Williams exited with his hamstring injury. He played the rest of Chicago’s 10 offensive snaps to conclude the contest, going 5-of-9 passing for 54 yards.

Keenum, 38, has not appeared in a game since he started two for Houston back in 2023. He was 34-of-53 in those two contests for 291 yards with a touchdown and three interceptions.

Keenum has appeared in 80 games with 66 starts in his career, dating back to 2013.

The Bears also have rookie Miller Moss at quarterback on their practice squad.

Playing Monday night, Chicago’s first injury report of Week 3 is due out on Thursday.

item.title: Klint Kubiak: I enjoy that our team's 2-0, but no one's made the playoffs going 2-0
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: There might be a little something brewing with the Raiders.
item.content:encoded:
There might be a little something brewing with the Raiders.

The club has started 2-0 for the first time since 2021. Klint Kubiak is the first head coach to begin his tenure with the franchise 2-0 since Bill Callahan back in 2002.

But Kubiak isn't putting too much stock in the team's hot start.

“I enjoy that our team is 2-0, our organization is 2-0,” Kubiak said in his Monday press conference, via transcript from the team. “No one's made the playoffs going 2-0.”

Still, when beginning a head coaching tenure, a hot start is particularly valuable.

“I think it just reinforces the messages that we've been sending,” Kubiak said. "Our guys have been very coachable, and our guys want to win. Winning is important to this team, it’s important to this coaching staff. We also have very short memories and know that you can only win one at a time.

“And so, we're turning the page, and now we get to prepare to play a really good Saints team.”

After a game at home and a game in Los Angeles with a favorable crowd, the Raiders will travel to New Orleans to take on the Saints for what could be a sneaky good game in Week 3.

item.title: Mike Macdonald's comments about Sean Payton weren't intended for public consumption
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald launched his career as a head coach with a win over Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald launched his career as a head coach with a win over Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos. The game from September 2024 moved back to the front burner on Tuesday, thanks to footage from Macdonald's recent interview with Graham Bensinger.

The excerpt, which wasn't released when the first clips and quotes began to be circulated, relates to a squabble that emerged regarding the use by the Seahawks of fan-generated video from Broncos training-camp practices. It got ugly, as Macdonald told the story to Bensinger.

It could get ugly between the Seahawks and Bensinger's camp. As we understand it, the conversation was not intended by Macdonald for public consumption. The Seahawks, we're told, didn't even know that portion of the "more off than on" the record discussion had been recorded until Tuesday morning.

The situation is another reminder that everything is potentially on the record, absent a clear agreement between the parties that it's not. And while Bensinger's people didn't breach any journalistic rules by using it, the fact that it was posted could make future subjects more leery about agreeing to be interviewed.

On or off the record, others are befuddled by Macdonald's decision to air gripes from two years ago. And there's a question as to whether the various things Macdonald said to Bensinger (regarding Payton and others) are the product of arrogance or naiveté.

"What's the point?" said one source connected to neither the Seahawks nor the Broncos. "It was reckless."

The Broncos declined comment on the situation. Undoubtedly, Payton will be asked about it when he conducts his usual Wednesday press conference.

Either way, the kerfuffle adds a little extra sizzle to a spicy Week 6 Thursday night game between the two teams.

item.title: Report: Jaxson Dart's injury could be season-ending
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: MRI brings bad news for the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
One day after an apparently serious injury to Bears starting quarterback Caleb Williams ended up being not nearly as bad as it seemed, an injury to Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart has turned out to be far worse than believed.

Via NFL Network, an MRI showed that Dart's knee injury is worse than expected. He's now expected to be out an extended period of time, and possibly for the rest of the season.

It's very bad news for a team that showed great promise in Week 1, and it moves Jameis Winston into the starting job. He struggled in relief of Dart on Monday night, completing 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception.

The Giants have no other quarterbacks on the 53-man roster; Jake Haener is on the practice squad. Which means that the Giants will likely be scouring all available options for another player at the position — from free agency to a potential trade with a team that has a surplus at the position.

Originally, it was believed that Dart had an MCL sprain. Coach John Harbaugh told reporters on Monday night that the injury was in that "neighborhood." Clearly, it wasn't.

item.title: John Harbaugh gets another chance to consider Colin Kaepernick
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When Colin Kaepernick was being ignored by the NFL teams, he didn't have much to say.
item.content:encoded:
When Colin Kaepernick was being ignored by the NFL teams, he didn't have much to say. Now that he's selling a book, interviews with Kaepernick are popping up everywhere.

We haven't paid much attention to his various sit-downs and sound bites because, frankly, it's an old story. The NFL has long since moved on from Kaepernick, freezing him out long enough to make it unrealistic that the now-38-year-old quarterback would have a plausible path to a roster, a practice squad, or even a tryout.

Still, one news item caught our eye in recent weeks. With Kaepernick's book tour putting him back in the vicinity of the front burner, Giants coach John Harbaugh told Ian O'Connor of The Athletic that Harbaugh wanted to add Kaepernick to the Ravens in 2017.

Through it all, Kaepernick got one workout, five years ago with the Raiders. With the Giants now desperate for quarterback help (and with Jake Haener and Brandon Allen as the most viable options behind new starter Jameis Winston), why not bring Kaepernick in for a look?

Kaepernick continues to say that he's staying in shape, and that he wants to play. It should be immediately obvious whether he still has the abilities that made Harbaugh interested in him nine years ago.

Harbaugh's New York staff includes Greg Roman, who was the offensive coordinator during Kaepernick's first four years in San Francisco. It would be easy, in theory, to configure the offense to fit Kaepernick. If Kaepernick still has the skills he had when he last played.

It starts with a workout (and quite possibly ends with one). There's no reason not to give it a whirl. The anthem controversy has subsided. (Harbaugh and the Giants surely would want assurances that Kaepernick wouldn't dust it off, if he ended up on the sideline before games.)

The threshold question is how does Kaepernick look? And there's only one way to find out. The Giants, who now face not having Jaxson Dart for up to the rest of the season, have plenty of reasons to give Kaepernick a chance to show them what he can do.

It would be different if John Harbaugh hadn't recently spoken in such glowing terms about Kaepernick. With not many viable options available in free agency — and with Harbaugh having considerable power in New York — let's see if Harbaugh puts his recent words into current action.

item.title: John Harbaugh on Jaxson Dart: Evaluations ongoing, no final decisions yet
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: A report on Tuesday indicated Dart may miss the rest of the season with a knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
Giants head coach John Harbaugh isn't ready to make any announcements about the extent of quarterback Jaxson Dart's knee injury.

A report on Tuesday indicated that an MRI showed more damage than doctors initially believed Dart sustained early in Monday night's loss to the Rams and that he could be out for the rest of the season. Harbaugh spoke to reporters on a videoconference shortly after that report and said that the team is still working to determine next steps with their starter.

"I’m not sure exactly what news or how anything’s been stated," Harbaugh said, via SNY. "Right now, evaluations are ongoing. We haven't got any final decisions yet, we've learned a lot more. I wouldn't want to share too much until decisions get made and that takes more than one person."

Harbaugh said that the team has confidence in Jameis Winston, but Harbaugh said it's "pretty self-evident" that losing a starting quarterback is a big blow to what the team would like to achieve this season.

item.title: Report: Giants could re-sign Brandon Allen as their third QB
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: With Jaxson Dart's injury worse than expected, Jameis Winston will become the Giants' starting quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
With Jaxson Dart's injury worse than expected, Jameis Winston will become the Giants' starting quarterback. The team, though, is in the market for a third quarterback.

Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that the Giants could re-sign Brandon Allen.

They have Jake Haener on the practice squad.

Allen, 34, has spent five of the past six seasons with Giants quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan. He backed up Cam Ward with the Titans last season.

Allen, though, struggled in three preseason games, going 26-of-38 for 224 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions.

He has played 19 games with 10 starts in his career, completing 56.7 percent of his passes for 1,882 yards with 11 touchdowns and nine interceptions. He has made at least one start for the Broncos, Bengals and 49ers.

item.title: Vikings are now the betting favorites to win the NFC North
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Heading into the season, the Vikings were a distant fourth in the betting odds to win the NFC North.
item.content:encoded:
Heading into the season, the Vikings were a distant fourth in the betting odds to win the NFC North. A lot can change in two weeks.

The Vikings are now 2-0, with both wins coming against division opponents, a game ahead of the Lions, Packers and Bears, and the new betting favorites to win the division.

The Vikings' odds are +194 to win what looks to be the NFL's most competitive division. The Lions are next at +205, followed by the Packers at +285. Last year's NFC North winners, the Bears, not have the longest odds, at +500, amid concerns that Caleb Williams could miss extended time with a hamstring injury.

Uncertainty at quarterback in Minnesota is an issue, but the Vikings have found a way to win two weeks in a row with Carson Wentz replacing the injured Kyler Murray. The Vikings' defense looks ferocious, and the Vikings look like a playoff team. Something few thought they'd be just a couple weeks ago.

item.title: Through two weeks, four starting quarterbacks have been injured
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 2023 season featured more than a few serious quarterback injuries.
item.content:encoded:
The 2023 season featured more than a few serious quarterback injuries. The 2026 season has started with four of 32 starters suffering injuries during the first two weeks of action.

In Week 1, the Seahawks lost quarterback Sam Darnold for at least one game with a glute injury. (He could be back in Week 3.) In Week 2, Bears quarterback Caleb Williams pulled a hamstring and is week-to-week. In the late-afternoon window, Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow, again. On Monday night, Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart sustained what is believed to be an MCL sprain.

More recently, the next man up in Chicago (Tyson Bagent) has landed in the concussion protocol.

The situation highlights an ever-present risk when it comes to playing football. Quarterbacks get hit, in all sorts of ways — after weeks of practice in which they're insulated from contact.

As Mike Tomlin said in Week 1, the inability to hit quarterbacks in practice put defenses at a disadvantage. The quarterbacks are at a disadvantage, too; they've gone from bubble wrap to fair game.

On Monday's Let's Go!, North Carolina coach Bill Belichick (who is far chattier than he is during games) suggested that limited padded practices make it harder for the blockers and, in turn, the quarterbacks.

“The offensive line has really gotten shortchanged because they're not in pads very often," Belichick said. "Basically 20 times a year, 10 in training camp, 10 during the regular season. And I think 20 practices is just not really enough for those guys to develop their skills. And the defensive players are ahead of them and offensive lineman gets beaten and you know who's getting hit. And so I think one thing that would really help the situation would be some type of developmental program for offensive linemen who don't play. Not saying guys that have played 16 games, but talking about guys that don't play, that need that development coming into the NFL and type athletes they face and pass protection and blitz pick[up] and all that. It's so involved and so difficult that I think that would help the quarterback’s longevity as much as anything."

Even with a highly competent offensive line, a quarterback is always one play away from taking a big hit, and possibly from being injured. And nothing can change a team's fortunes faster than losing their starting quarterback.

UPDATE 9:10 p.m. ET: Actually, the number is five. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a concussion on the third drive of the Week 1 win over the Packers. Carson Wentz replaced Murray, who has been cleared for Week 3.

item.title: Tua Tagovailoa returns to full participation at Falcons practice
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Tua Tagovailoa won't be starting for the Falcons on Thursday night, but he could suit up for the first time this season.
item.content:encoded:
Tua Tagovailoa won't be starting for the Falcons on Thursday night, but he could suit up for the first time this season.

The Falcons listed Tagovailoa as a full participant in practice on Tuesday for the first time since he suffered an oblique injury during a practice ahead of Week 1. The Falcons already announced that Michael Penix will make his 2026 debut as their starter against the Packers this week and Tagovailoa could be their backup ahead of Cooper Rush and Jack Strand.

Rush started the first two games and Strand replaced him in the second half of Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Panthers.

Defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring) was the only player listed as out of practice Tuesday. The Falcons also put cornerback A.J. Terrell (groin) on injured reserve earlier in the day.

Cornerback Billy Bowman (Achilles), tight end Nick Muse (shoulder), right tackle Jawaan Taylor (rib), defensive end Brandon Dorlus (thumb), running back Brian Robinson (ankle), and defensive lineman LaCale London (hip) were listed as full participants.

item.title: UFL puts Houston and Birmingham teams in Rhode Island and Colorado
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Houston and Birmingham are out.
item.content:encoded:
Houston and Birmingham are out. Pawtucket and Colorado Springs are in.

The UFL announced on Wednesday that the teams moved from existing markets will be relocated to Rhode Island and Colorado for 2027.

The spring league reiterated the plan to expand to 10 teams in 2028, with Utah and Oklahoma joining the operation.

“2026 was an incredible year for the UFL, and seeing the response from our fans, players, and partners has made what comes next even more exciting,” UFL co-owner Mike Repole said in a press release. “There is a real energy around this league right now, and we’re thrilled to bring that energy to four new markets. We said in July that our next step was finding the right markets, venues, and fan bases where we can work with local leaders to build the strongest franchises for today and for the future, and we believe Colorado, Rhode Island, Oklahoma, and Utah represent those qualities. We’re thankful to the local leaders and partners who believed in this vision and have helped us get here. We can’t wait to see these markets come to life and the best part is that this is just the beginning.”

Colorado will host its first game on Sunday, April 11st Weidner Field in Colorado Springs. Rhode Island gets its home slate rolling on Friday, April 2, at Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket.

The nicknames, colors, and logos for the relocated teams will be revealed next month. Which means they won't keep the existing names that date back to the original USFL — the Gamblers and the Stallions.

item.description: The Panthers will be without Jonathon Brooks for an extended period of time and they're set to kick the tires on a veteran running back as they work to fill out their backfield in Brooks's absence.
item.content:encoded:
The Panthers will be without Jonathon Brooks for an extended period of time and they're set to kick the tires on a veteran running back as they work to fill out their backfield in Brooks's absence.

Austin Ekeler will try out for the club on Wednesday, per a report from Aaron Wilson that has been confirmed by multiple other outlets. Ekeler has not played since tearing his Achilles while with the Commanders last September.

Ekeler was in his second season with Washington after spending his first seven years in the league with the Chargers. He was a dual threat throughout his time with the Chargers, and peaked with 3,195 yards from scrimmage and 38 touchdowns across the 2021 and 2022 seasons.

Brooks is expected to miss more than a month after having core muscle surgery. Chuba Hubbard and AJ Dillon are the other backs on the 53-man roster for Carolina.

item.title: Michael Penix: Being healthy was my target, I feel I'm where I want to be
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Michael Penix is set to make his first start for the Falcons since last November when the team faces the Packers on Thursday night and the quarterback shared his excitement about that return during a press conference on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Penix is set to make his first start for the Falcons since last November when the team faces the Packers on Thursday night and the quarterback shared his excitement about that return during a press conference on Tuesday.

Penix had said in recent weeks that he felt close to getting back in the lineup, but not all the way back to where he needed to be to feel confident in playing. He said that changed late last week as lingering soreness went away and he was convinced it was time to get back on the field after "pushing it to the limit" in a workout and finding that the knee "responded good."

Penix said that the timing of his return had nothing to do with having extended rest heading into Week 4 or because of how poorly the first two weeks have gone for the team.

“Being healthy is what I was targeting. I was never no week-to-week thing," Penix said at a press conference. "It was being healthy. Whenever I felt like I can go out there, like I said, get out of all that soreness and get stronger each and every day, that’s what it was always about. Once I felt healthy, it felt like I was ready to go. . . . I’m never gonna sit out if I’m healthy. I knew I wasn’t where I needed to be the first two weeks and now I feel like I’m where I want to be, so that’s why you’ll see me up this week."

Penix called it "very exciting when you make the final decision" and, given the way the offense has floundered through two games, he's likely not the only Falcons player excited about the change in plans for this week.

item.title: Derrick Henry says Ravens weren't good enough, but not complaining about lack of carries
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Ravens barely used Henry in the second half of their loss to the Saints.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens gave the ball to Derrick Henry nine times in the first quarter on Sunday against the Saints, and the last of those touches was a touchdown run that gave Baltimore a 7-0 lead. But as the game went on, Henry disappeared.

Even though the Ravens were leading for most of the game, Henry was hardly getting the ball. In the fourth quarter, when the Ravens went from a 17-9 lead to a 24-17 loss, Henry only got the ball once. Overall, Henry finished the game with 16 carries for 68 yards and three catches for 19 yards.

Henry wasn't complaining after the game about his lack of carries, but he did say the whole team needed to be better.

“We just weren’t good enough in the second half to win this game,” Henry said, via the Baltimore Sun. “We were put in a position to win this game. We just have to be better. We just weren’t good enough — at all.”

Asked if Henry wasn't getting the ball because he was injured, head coach Jesse Minter said nothing was wrong with Henry.

"Derrick was definitely himself," Minter said.

Minter acknowledged the Ravens are going to need to get better at playing with a lead.

“This team is going to have a lead [again],” Minter said. “We are going to continue to chase and learn from what happened in those situations. We will get better and put our guys in the best position to be successful given the circumstances.”

item.title: Alleged victim of Daejon Love says she reported him to 49ers in December 2025
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 49ers have said, via information previously provided by an unnamed team source to Kalyn Kahler of ESPN, that they did not know about Daejon Love, who allegedly posed as a player on the team as part of an elaborate scheme, until the FBI contacted the 49ers in August 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers have said, via information previously provided by an unnamed team source to Kalyn Kahler of ESPN, that they did not know about Daejon Love, who allegedly posed as a player on the team as part of an elaborate scheme, until the FBI contacted the 49ers in August 2026.

One of Daejon Love's alleged victims says otherwise.

Via Kahler, Gwen Herndon says she completed a “complaint/concern” form through the team's website on December 20, 2025.

In the message, Herndon said "there is a federal investigation surrounding a man pretending to be a 49ers player," and she named Love. She also said he stole money from women and that "he is severely damaging the reputation of your team."

"I wanted you to be aware of the situation and hopefully proactive in denouncing his involvement on your team," Herndon wrote to the 49ers.

She said she received a response from Levis Stadium guest services one week later.

"We take reports of individuals misrepresenting themselves as members of the San Francisco 49ers very seriously," the response said. "For safety and legal reasons, the team cannot comment on ongoing investigations or specific individuals. However, we appreciate you bringing this to our attention and encouraging proactive measures to protect the integrity of the organization.

"If you have information that could assist law enforcement or legal authorities, we encourage you to contact the appropriate agencies directly. Our internal team will also monitor any instances of impersonation and take action as appropriate to protect fans and the team's reputation. Thank you again for your vigilance and concern for the Niners community."

The 49ers declined to confirm to Kahler the existence of the exchange or to otherwise comment.

Love and his alleged partner, Taylor Chan, were arrested on August 24. Authorities contend they defrauded more than two dozen women out of approximately $1.3 million. Last week, Kahler reported that the actual number of victims may exceed 60.

Obviously, if the 49ers knew about Love, took no action, and the fraud continued until the arrests in August, that would be a problem for the team. While it may not create civil liability to anyone who was defrauded after December 20, 2025, it's a P.R. issue that would reflect very poorly on the organization.

item.title: Jerry Jones pushes back on idea of an expansion team in Europe
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In recent weeks, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has commented on multiple occasions regarding his "no doubt" belief that the NFL will have multiple teams in other countries — with Europe being the most likely destination.
item.content:encoded:
In recent weeks, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has commented on multiple occasions regarding his "no doubt" belief that the NFL will have multiple teams in other countries — with Europe being the most likely destination.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones doesn't see that happening through expansion of the league.

“I don’t know about an expansion," Jones said on 105.3 the Fan in Dallas, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing. "I see the games continuing like they are. And I see the ethos, if you will, of the game, the story of the game really expanding all over the world. But fundamentally, to have an expansion team, probably is pretty far. If it’s here, it’s in the future.”

It's unclear whether Jones was expressing pessimism about an international presence generally, or specifically through expansion. Absent adding new teams, the only way to put teams in Europe or elsewhere would be to relocate existing franchises. (Good luck identifying teams that would be viable candidates to move.)

Regardless, Goodell currently has more power than any one owner. And if Goodell sees an international team coming, it makes sense to take him seriously.

For years, the NFL has dangled the possibility of a team in London as part of the effort to build interest there. More recently, the talk feels like something more than pandering to Europe.

If it happens, it surely won't happen soon. At some point, however, the only way to truly export the passion that American fans feel for the sport will be to give fans in other countries a local team around which they can rally. London continues to be the most logical starting point, with one team playing home games at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and the other playing at Wembley Stadium.

Since the merger in 1970, the NFL hasn't had a dramatic uptick in teams at one time. Two were added in 1976 (Buccaneers and Seahawks). Two more were added in 1995 (Jaguars and Panthers). The Browns returned in 1999, after the Browns became the Ravens, and the Texans rounded out the league at 32 in 2002.

Twenty-four years later, the NFL is in the longest stretch in league history without the addition of a new team. At some point, it will grow. When it does, two new teams in London make the most sense.

item.title: Jonathan Owens, Simone Biles had their Porsche stolen in Chicago by "three men in masks"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In March, linebacker Jonathan Owens left the Bears in free agency for the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
In March, linebacker Jonathan Owens left the Bears in free agency for the Colts. Before Owens and his wife, gymnast Simone Biles, left Chicago, they found themselves the victims of a robbery.

In a video posted Tuesday on social media, Biles said that "three men in masks came to our house and stole my Porsche" before they moved out of Chicago.

The car was recovered.

It's not clear when the theft occurred. And while some have interpreted Biles's quotes to mean that their home was invaded, that's not entirely clear from her video.

Either way, it makes Owens the latest known NFL victim of a theft at his home.

Owens, 31, has played for the Cardinals, Texans, Packers, Bears, and Colts. He has appeared in 84 regular-season games with 35 starts.

item.title: Commanders-Cowboys delivers 27.3 million in late Sunday window
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A whole lot of people heard Tom Brady say "oh shit" and "piss missile" on Sunday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
A whole lot of people heard Tom Brady say "oh shit" and "piss missile" on Sunday afternoon. (Hey, if smoking weed on the air is fair game, anything goes.)

Fox's broadcast of Commanders-Cowboys in the late-afternoon window of the second Sunday of the 2026 season attracted 27.4 million viewers.

It was the most-watched NFL telecast of the season to date. And it had everything to do with the presence of the Cowboys.

Especially since the Commanders lost their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels, at the end of the first half. And the game ultimately was a blowout, with Dallas winning the game, 37-20.

CBS will get the benefit of the Cowboys bump on Sunday. The Week 3 game against the Ravens from Brazil will be televised in the late-afternoon window on Sunday.

The Cowboys' Week 4 game against the Texans inexplicably lands in the 1:00 p.m. ET window on Fox. The Week 5 Dallas game against the Buccaneers is set for Thursday night. In Week 6, the Cowboys face the Packers at Lambeau Field on Sunday night.

After that, the Cowboys visit the Eagles on Monday night to wrap up Week 7.

item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Based on the way the respective teams played in Week 1, many expected Sunday night's game between the Colts and Chiefs to be a snoozer.
item.content:encoded:
Based on the way the respective teams played in Week 1, many expected Sunday night's game between the Colts and Chiefs to be a snoozer. Instead, it was an overtime thriller.

The game attracted 24.3 million viewers on average for NBC and Peacock.

The audience, which peaked at 27.4 million between 9:15 and 9:30 p.m. ET, made it the most-watched Week 2 Sunday night game since 2015.

It was also the fourth highest figure for an overtime game in 21 seasons of Sunday Night Football on NBC. In that span, 22 Sunday night games have gone to overtime.

The Sunday night slate continues in five days, with the Broncos hosting the Rams.

item.title: Adam Vinatieri sets Guinness World Record for the highest FG
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Adam Vinatieri isn't in the NFL record book for the longest field goal, but he now is the Guinness World Record-holder for the highest field goal.
item.content:encoded:
Adam Vinatieri isn't in the NFL record book for the longest field goal, but he now is the Guinness World Record-holder for the highest field goal.

The Hall of Fame kicker made a field goal from an altitude of 11,332 feet (3,434 meters) above sea level in the Swiss Alps on Tuesday.

Vinatieri's record-setting kick took place at Jungfraujoch, known as the “Top of Europe,” on snow-covered ground with swirling winds. A Guinness World Records adjudicator was on hand to certify the achievement.

“Snow is simply part of my time with the Patriots,” Vinatieri said, via a team news release. “But kicking a field goal at 3,454 meters is something completely different from anything I've ever done. You feel the altitude with every breath you take. Your heart rate is different. Your rhythm is different. And no one can really tell you beforehand how it will affect the kick, because no one has done this before. The fact that we were able to set the record under these conditions makes me very proud.”

The event kicked off the Patriots’ countdown to their Nov. 15 game in Munich and celebrated Vinatieri’s legendary career.

He last kicked in the NFL in 2019, retiring as the NFL’s all-time leader with 599 field goals.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The 49ers are adding a veteran wide receiver to their practice squad.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers are adding a veteran wide receiver to their practice squad.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that they will sign Brandin Cooks. Cooks recently worked out for the Ravens, but he'll join a 49ers receiving corps that's been riddled with injuries.

Demarcus Robinson sprained his ankle in Week 2 and Mike Evans suffered a hip injury in the win over the Dolphins. The 49ers were already without Ricky Pearsall, who is out for the season, and De'Zhaun Stribling, who will miss a couple of months after having ankle surgery.

Cooks played for the Saints and Bills last season, and he was the intended target on the interception that helped the Broncos eliminate Buffalo in the playoffs. He's also played for the Cowboys, Texans, Rams and Patriots since entering the league as a Saints first-rounder in 2014.

Cooks has 734 catches for 9,811 yards and 60 touchdowns over the course of his career.

item.title: Jayden Reed back in Green Bay, "too early" to tell if he'll play again this season
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed has returned to Green Bay.
item.content:encoded:
Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed has returned to Green Bay.

Reed remained in a New Jersey hospital after suffering a neck injury in Sunday's overtime win over the Jets. Head coach Matt LaFleur said that Reed is still undergoing tests on the injury and that conversations about whether he'll play again this season will have to wait.

“It’s way too early for that right now. . . . He’s got a lot going on," LaFleur said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com.

Reed missed 10 games with injuries last season and signed a three-year contract extension this offseason.

Reed was injured on the Packers' second offensive play of the game and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele was carted off on the next play. Bako-Bewele said on Tuesday that he will miss the rest of the year with a torn patellar tendon.

item.description: With punter Brett Thorson set to miss some time with a hamstring injury, the Vikings have added a veteran punter to their practice squad.
item.content:encoded:
With punter Brett Thorson set to miss some time with a hamstring injury, the Vikings have added a veteran punter to their practice squad.

Minnesota announced the team has signed Johnny Hekker to the unit.

Hekker, 35, spent the offseason program and training camp with Minnesota.

He spent the 2025 season with Tennessee, averaging 46.8 yards per punt with a 40.3-yard net average.

A four-time AP first-team All-Pro, Hekker has appeared in 229 career games for the Rams, Panthers, and Titans.

A fake punt specialist, Hekker has also completed 15-of-26 career passes for 193 yards with a touchdown.

The Vikings also signed running back Jaret Patterson to their practice squad and released receiver Trayvon Rudolph and cornerback Bryce Phillips from their practice squad.
